papers.title: Characterization of the in Vitro Osteogenic Response to Submicron TiO
papers.abstract: Titanium oxide (TiO2) nano-/microparticles have been widely used in orthopedic and dental sciences because of their excellent mechanical properties, chemical stability, and ability to promote the osseointegration of implants. However, how the structure and crystallinity of TiO2 particles may affect their osteogenic activity remains elusive. Herein, we evaluated the osteogenic response to submicron amorphous, anatase, and rutile TiO2 particles with controlled size and morphology. First, the ability of TiO2 particles to precipitate apatite was assessed in an acellular medium by using a simulated body fluid (SBF). Three days after the addition to SBF, anatase and rutile TiO2 particles induced the precipitation of aggregates of nanoparticles with a platelike morphology, typical for biomimetic apatite. Conversely, amorphous TiO2 particles induced the precipitation of particles with poor Ca/P atomic ratio only after 14 days of exposure to SBF. Next, the osteogenic response to TiO2 particles was assessed in vitro by incubating MC3T3-E1 preosteoblasts with the particles. The viability and mineralization efficiency of osteoblastic cells were maintained in the presence of all the tested TiO2 particles despite the differences in the induction of apatite precipitation in SBF by TiO2 particles with different structures. Analysis of the particles' surface charge and of the proteins adsorbed onto the particles from the culture media suggested that all the tested TiO2 particles acquired a similar biological identity in the culture media. We posited that this phenomenon attenuated potential differences in osteoblast response to amorphous, anatase, and rutile particles. Our study provides an important insight into the complex relationship between the physicochemical properties and function of TiO2 particles and sheds light on their safe use in medicine.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究TiO2颗粒的成骨反应，与LPBF制造和力学性能无关。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on TiO2 particle-induced osteogenic response, with no LPBF fabrication, no porous implant structure, no stress shielding analysis, no mechanical testing (static or fatigue), and no surface roughness characterization of as-built AM parts.

summary_zh.motivation: 评估TiO2颗粒结构晶型对成骨活性的影响。
summary_zh.method: 用无细胞SBF和MC3T3-E1细胞评估不同晶型TiO2颗粒的矿化和成骨反应。
summary_zh.result: 不同晶型TiO2颗粒在SBF中诱导磷灰石能力不同，但在细胞实验中成骨反应无显著差异。
summary_zh.validation: 体外细胞实验和无细胞矿化实验。

summary_en.motivation: To evaluate how the structure and crystallinity of TiO2 particles affect their osteogenic activity.
summary_en.method: Apatite formation in SBF and in vitro osteoblast response were assessed for amorphous, anatase, and rutile TiO2 particles.
summary_en.result: Anatase and rutile induced apatite faster than amorphous, but all particles supported comparable osteoblast viability and mineralization.
summary_en.validation: In vitro cell culture with MC3T3-E1 preosteoblasts and acellular SBF assay.

papers.title: Fabrication of Microspheres from High-Viscosity Bioink Using a Novel Microfluidic-Based 3D Bioprinting Nozzle.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting is a novel technology utilizing biocompatible materials, cells, drugs, etc. as basic microcomponents to form 3D artificial structures and is believed as a promising method for regenerative medicine. Droplet-based bioprinting can precisely generate microspheres and manipulate them into organized structures with high fidelity. Biocompatible hydrogels are usually used as bioinks in 3D bioprinting, however, the viscosity of the bioink could be increased due to the additives such as cells, drugs, nutrient factors and other functional polymers in some particular applications, making it difficult to form monodispersed microspheres from high-viscosity bioink at the orifice of the nozzle. In this work, we reported a novel microfluidic-based printing nozzle to prepare monodispersed microspheres from high-viscosity bioink using the phase-inversion method. Different flowing conditions can be achieved by changing the flow rates of the fluids to form monodispersed solid and hollow microspheres using the same nozzle. The diameter of the microspheres can be tuned by changing the flow rate ratio and the size distribution of the microspheres is narrow. The prepared calcium alginate microspheres could also act as micro-carriers in drug delivery.

llm.why_not_core: No AI/ML integration, no autonomous decision-making, purely a mechanical nozzle design.

summary_zh.motivation: 解决高粘度生物墨水在打印喷嘴处难以形成单分散微球的问题。
summary_zh.method: 采用基于相转化法的微流控喷嘴，通过调节流速比控制微球尺寸。
summary_zh.result: 成功制备出直径可调、分布窄的单分散实心和空心海藻酸钙微球。
summary_zh.validation: 通过显微镜观察微球形态并统计尺寸分布进行验证。

summary_en.motivation: To address the difficulty of forming monodispersed microspheres from high-viscosity bioink at the nozzle orifice.
summary_en.method: A microfluidic-based printing nozzle using phase inversion to generate microspheres, with diameter controlled by flow rate ratio.
summary_en.result: Monodispersed solid and hollow calcium alginate microspheres with tunable diameter and narrow size distribution were fabricated.
summary_en.validation: Experimental characterization of microsphere morphology and size distribution via microscopy.
